tests.description: [pto] Hannah requests a week off in December (store peak period)

vars.question: How do I request a week off in December?

tests.description: [pto] Hannah's year-end PTO balance and carryover (calculation)

vars.question: How much PTO will I have by December 31, and how much carries over into next year?

assert.value: Facts: balance 88 hours as of Oct 24, 2026; she accrues 6 hours per biweekly pay period (full-time, 7 completed years); 4 pay periods end between Oct 25 and Dec 31 (periods 22-25), giving 112 hours, or 104 hours after her 8 approved hours on Nov 27. Full-time carryover is 80 hours, so about 24 hours would be forfeited (32 if she does not use the approved 8 hours). Pass if the reply's projection is 112 and/or 104 (or a clearly explained close variant that counts pay period 26), states the 80-hour carryover cap, and warns that hours above 80 are forfeited. Fail if it uses the wrong accrual rate or omits forfeiture.

Optional: using PTO lets accrual resume; only 80 hours carry over. Fail if it projects 7 hours per pay period through year-end without applying the cap.

tests.description: [pto] Part-time employee with 18 years of service: accrual rate and year-end balance (calculation)

vars.question: How much PTO do I earn each pay period, and how much will I have by the end of the year?

sections: When your PTO accrual rate changes

assert.value: Facts: Elise is hourly part-time (25 hours per week, under 30) and was hired February 20, 2008, so she has 18 completed years of service. Part-time employees with 15 or more years accrue 3.5 hours per biweekly pay period (91 hours per year). Her balance was 31.5 hours as of October 24, 2026, with no approved time off. Pay periods 22 to 25 end by December 31, so she will have 45.5 hours (49 if the reply also counts pay period 26, which ends January 2, 2027, and says so). She stays under the 80-hour part-time cap. Required: gives 3.5 hours per pay period and a year-end balance of 45.5 (or the explained 49). Optional: part-time employees can carry over at most 40 hours into 2027, so about 5.5 hours would be forfeited if unused. Fail if it uses the full-time rate (7 hours), a lower tenure tier (2.0, 2.5 or 3.0 hours), or says she can carry over 80 hours.
